items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: late '44, I played several weeks, maybe two months with Don Byas, our trio, with Clyde Hart on piano and I think, if memory doesn't fail me it was Teddy Sturgis on bass.

ctx.x: I would like to get along to my association with Don Byas, another legend in his time, in our time, rather. And Ben Webster. First I'll take Don, because it follows in sequence that late '44, I played several weeks, maybe two months with Don Byas, our trio, with Clyde Hart on piano and I think, if memory doesn't fail me it was Teddy Sturgis on bass.
Of course in this band with Ted Sturgis on bass, you playing drums; of course Don Byas was a great tenor saxophone player, like Ben Webster -- also a great tenor saxophone player, huh, Cliff?

However, the other band with a young new piano player from Pittsburgh -- was Errol Garner and Slam Stewart was the leader, and wonderfully talented Harold West on drums. He did lovely brush work, and utilized a new sound to me by accenting the heavy part with the stick and the bell with a large cymbal. A little of that rubbed off on me along the way.
